RESPONSE_TO: CC2  
Your CC2_F009 addresses the concern if “specialist clustering” means diversity is created inside one model slot while preserving a single external emission. My earlier concern was not specifically inter-model topology; it was redundant generalist search over the same space. Runner-side sub-agents do address that redundancy, but only if the merge layer canonicalizes by root cause before the shared registry. Without pre-registry dedup, it recreates the same churn one layer earlier.

CONFIRM ChatGPT_F001  
EXTEND ChatGPT_F001 | Gamma advisory should be computed on cumulative unique target-code findings, but stop/continue must key off open-state counts partitioned by severity and by harness-vs-target scope.

CONFIRM ChatGPT_F003

CONFIRM ChatGPT_F004

CHALLENGE ChatGPT_F002 | The 8-round recommendation is under-justified against the observed tail.
Evidence: Exp 31 still produced 5 and 7 novel findings in R13-R14 after the R7 intervention, so an 8-round hard default risks truncating unresolved HIGH/CRITICAL carryover unless the stop rule is explicitly state-gated rather than budget-gated.

CHALLENGE Gemini_G_F006 | 5 rounds is not supported by the artifact.
Evidence: Exp 31 post-intervention novelty did not collapse immediately; R7-R10 were [4,5,5,6] novel findings. A 5-round cap would end before the observed stabilization window and before closure machinery has time to contract the registry.

CHALLENGE Gemini_G_F008 | Restricting gamma to only CRITICAL/HIGH is too brittle for PoC convergence measurement.
Evidence: HIL’s verified residual set in Exp 31 was dominated by LOW/MEDIUM verification edge cases plus harness issues. A critical-only gamma can show apparent convergence while materially open target-code work remains. Severity should gate termination, not define the only discovery series.

CHALLENGE CC2_F007 | Full-mesh retention is not supported by the communication data.
Evidence: 1.26M chars, 2.9% cross-model reference overhead, and zero CHALLENGEs indicate the full transcript exchange was mostly unused as an action channel. Shared registry state, not raw peer prose, is the missing primitive.

CONFIRM CC2_F008

CONFIRM CC2_F009

CHALLENGE CC2_F011 | kappa > 0.6 as a hard convergence gate is under-supported.
Evidence: Exp 31 already had kappa = 0.619 while closure was broken and churn remained 58.3%. Kappa is useful diagnostics, not a sufficient stop component.

FIND: The core design change is to stop treating cumulative discovery math as a proxy for closure.  
FIX: The concrete replacements are a state-based stop rule, star/blackboard registry, 3+escalation reviewer architecture, internal-only CC2 specialization, 8-round default with extension to 10, dual finding schemas, and telemetry-only gamma/kappa.  
FOLLOW: These fixes are coupled. Adopting only one in isolation will not solve Exp 31’s failure mode. The minimum coherent package is F001+F002+F006; the efficiency package is F003+F004+F005; F007 prevents reintroducing unjustified hard gates. Definitive stance: convergence likely already occurred qualitatively in Exp 31, and the next experiment should be designed to detect state contraction rather than wait for cumulative gamma to do a job it cannot do.
